text: Cameras record events ranging from intimate family scenes to quiet twilight scenes. Two primary mechanisms regulate light intake: the aperture controls incoming volume while the shutter manages reflection duration. A wide aperture admits greater illumination, permitting varied brightness levels. Conversely, a narrower opening enhances texture and dimensional depth; note that higher f-numbers indicate this smaller setting. Shutter speed dictates how long the sensor remains active. Together these variables define exposure, a foundational requirement for producing high-quality images.
